task_instance: Give a high-level summary of a local Git repository (recent commits, top contributors, file count) by running scripts/analyze_repo.py against the repo path, as the skill instructs.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is produced only by executing the bundled Python script scripts/analyze_repo.py (and get_changed_files.py), which shells out via subprocess to the git command-line tool to read commit logs, contributors and tracked-file counts. The office-assistant runtime cannot run code, scripts, or shell commands of any kind and cannot invoke git, so the script cannot be executed and its JSON data source cannot be produced. The run rules forbid writing a replacement/stub for a bundled script or fabricating the data it would return, so there is no permitted path to the deliverable. The bundled scripts themselves are present next to SKILL.md (so this is not a missing-skill-file issue); the missing ability is code/command execution.
evidence: Read SKILL.md: skill instructs running `python scripts/analyze_repo.py "/path/to/repo"` and `python scripts/get_changed_files.py "/path/to/repo"`, parsing the returned JSON. Glob of the skill dir confirmed both scripts/analyze_repo.py and scripts/get_changed_files.py exist. Read analyze_repo.py confirmed it uses subprocess.run([...]) to call the git CLI (git log, git shortlog, git ls-files) with cwd=repo_path and prints json.dumps(result); requires a real .git repository and a runnable python+git. Runtime grants only text file read/write/edit and web fetch/search, explicitly no code/shell execution, so neither building a sample repo nor running the analyzer is possible. No result file produced beyond this record.
